question.leadin: Answer the following about Douglas MacArthur.
question.text: Truman dismissed Douglas MacArthur and replaced him with Matthew Ridgway during this war. MacArthur led a surprise amphibious landing at Incheon (IN-chon) during this war.
question.clue: Task Force Faith was disbanded after losing a battle on the east side of the Chosin Reservoir in this war, but U.S. marines to the south fought out of a Chinese encirclement.

swap.text: A major turning point in the war was the arrival of Communist Chinese troops, who crossed this river on the border of North Korea and China to enter the fray.
swap.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

question.leadin: After conducting "literati purges" against members of the Sarim faction, one emperor banned an alphabet used in this peninsula to suppress criticism of his regime.
question.text: Name this East Asian peninsula, once home to the kingdom of Joseon ["JOH-sun"]. This peninsula juts off of modern-day Russia and China and is separated from Japan by a namesake strait.
question.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about one of the Four Asian Tigers.
swap.text: This peninsular country with capital at Seoul includes other cities such as Incheon and Pusan.
swap.answerHtml: South Korea [accept Republic of Korea or Korea Republic; prompt on Korea]
swap.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

question.text: During the lead up to this time period, the forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire ships to turn back the much larger force of Cao Cao at the Battle of Red Cliffs. This time period followed the collapse of the Han dynasty.
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the abolition of slavery throughout the world.
swap.text: This dynasty abolished slavery in Korea as part of the Gabo Reforms in 1894. This dynasty declared Korea an empire in 1897; however, it would be annexed to the Japanese empire in 1910.
swap.clue: Members of the yangban (yong-bon) class were killed by followers of the "Eastern Learning" Donghak religion during this dynasty.

question.leadin: U.S. naval forces have been involved in multiple incidents in Asia. answer the following.
question.text: In 1968, the USS Pueblo was attacked by vessels from this country off of Ryo Island near Wonsan. That country still holds the Pueblo to this day in its Victorious War Museum.
question.clue: A 2019 Summit between the U.S. and this nation hosted in Hanoi ended after a request to destroy the Yongbyon nuclear facility was refused by minister Ri Yong-ho.

swap.leadin: This leader was referred to as "supreme leader", as well as "Dear Leader" and "Generalissimo"
swap.text: Identify this leader of North Korea from 1994 to 2011. He died on December 17, 2011 of a heart attack.
swap.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

question.leadin: Among this man's domestic accomplishments include granting serfs a form of maternity leave and backing the development of the world's first rain gauge.
question.text: Identify this fourth ruler of Korea's Joseon (JOH-sun) dynasty whose establishment of the 28-letter hangul script is still celebrated on an October holiday.
question.clue: It was said that an innovation from this monarch's reign could be learnt by wise men in a morning and by stupid men in ten days.

swap.leadin: The decks of ships of this type were covered with iron spikes in order to prevent enemies from boarding them.
swap.text: Name this type of ship, which was among the first armored ships in the world and may have been covered with iron. They had a dragon head at the prow, from which a cannon could be fired or smoke released.
swap.clue: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.

question.leadin: Name these Asian politicians who had European wives.
question.text: This first president of South Korea assumed dictatorial powers when the Korean War broke out, and was exiled with his Austrian wife Franziska Donner to Hawaii after his overthrow in a 1960 coup.
question.clue: This ruler, who put down the Jeju uprising at the beginning of his rule, was forced into exile in Hawaii by the 1960 April Revolution, and he was replaced by Yun Bosun.

swap.text: This man led North Korea during the Korean War. Despite dying in 1994, he continues to hold the title of "Eternal President" of North Korea.
swap.clue: This man's government was involved in conflict with the U.S. in the Axe Murder Incident and the capture of the Pueblo.

question.text: The Chinese invaded Goguryeo following calls for aid from this kingdom located in the peninsula's south. This kingdom, along with Gorguryeo and Baekje ("peck-jay"), was one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.leadin: This naval commander destroyed approximately 100 enemy ships at the Battle of Hansan Island without losing a single ship of his own.
swap.text: Name this admiral who leveraged the regular reversal of the tide to win the Battle of Myeongnyang ("myung-nyahng"). This undefeated Korean admiral used turtle ships to defend Korea during the Imjin War.

question.leadin: The Haerye ("HEH-r'yeh") commentary helps explain how to use this system, whose creation is commemorated by a national holiday on October 9.
question.text: Name this system said to be easy enough to understand that even a stupid man could learn how to use it in ten days.
question.answerHtml: Hangul [or Hangeul; or Chosongeul; accept Korean alphabet or Korean script; prompt on Korean; prompt on alphabet or script]
question.clue: This alphabet is transliterated using the McCune-Reischauer system, and was banned under a cultural assimilation policy before the outbreak of World War II.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about naval engagements in Asian history.
swap.text: Japan's own attempts at navy-driven expansionism met with similar disaster after the turtle ships of this revered Korean admiral bested the fleet of Toyotomi Hideyoshi at the Battle of Noryang Point.
swap.clue: This admiral was undefeated in all naval engagements, although he died during the Battle of Noryang, which saw the Japanese finally repelled.

question.text: Chaebols have historically obtained preferential loans from the South Korean government through bribery, such as the 45 billion dollars given to Park Geun-hye by this de facto leader of Samsung, who served less than one year of a five-year prison sentence.

swap.text: Original language term required. The Hanjungrok claims that Crown Prince Sado suffered from a "phobia" of this clothing, often burning many outfits. Modern examples of this traditional class of clothing were modeled on Joseon-era outfits.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a period in Korean history.
question.text: In 1419, Yi Jong-mu was chosen by the Choson king Sejong to lead this invasion against the Wokou pirates on Tsushima Island. It ended with the signing of a treaty between Choson and the So clan, who lived on Tsushima.

swap.text: This founder of Korean science, who was able to enter the civil service under Sejong due to the removal of class barriers on government workers, invented the Chegugi, an early rain gauge, as well as an improved sundial and water clock, though his downfall came when he provided the king with a faulty sedan chair.
